items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They should be playing Thelonious Monk.

ctx.x: What do you think that the repertory movement in jazz should be doing?
They should be playing Thelonious Monk. That’s for sure. They should be playing Tadd Dameron. There’s Kenny Dorham. There’s a lot of music there that’s really fantastic that nobody’s playing.
Should they be playing it – should they be replicating what has been done, or should they be finding the music inside the music?

items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: you played Thelonious Monk and you don’t have it on here

ctx.x: Have you had good or bad luck dealing with record companies over the years?

Well in a way you can look at it two ways. It was good that you got to record as far as the popularity is concerned. But record companies have a very strange business ethic. Very strange. And it isn’t good for the artist. And I haven’t understood yet what it is that they’re trying to achieve. It looks like they’re mainly building up a catalogue and then selling it. That seems to be what they’re — they never seem to try to keep the record company building in a way that it’s going to last. Because for some reason…
These are representatives of those organizations?
